evidence_against: The broader 12h, 24h, and 72h return sequences remain positive for BTC (1.07%, 7.59%, and 8.91%), ETH (7.74%, 17.81%, and 18.28%), and ETH/BTC (6.62%, 9.49%, and 8.61%).
Breadth remains broad and unchanged in aggregate: 75 advancers out of 100 and a 75% advance ratio in both captures; decliners increased only from 7 to 8.
ETH/BTC closed above 0.03 for 13 consecutive hourly closes and remains above that level, contradicting a broad deterioration in ETH relative performance.

Latest taker quote imbalance is positive for BTC (+0.377) and ETH (+0.320), while the displayed-depth signal is negative; this within-microstructure disagreement weakens a one-sided bearish interpretation.
BTC open interest declined 0.18% between owner captures, whereas a persistent leverage-led continuation of the pullback signal is not established from the supplied observations.
evidence_for: The latest 4h sequence is negative across BTC (-0.32%), ETH (-0.49%), and ETH/BTC (-0.18%) after large positive 12h-to-72h moves, establishing short-horizon deceleration.
Between the prior and latest captures, BTC and ETH marks declined 0.51% and 0.64%; their spot midpoints and VWAPs also declined.
BTC displayed depth20 quote-notional imbalance deteriorated from -0.245 to -0.802. ETH displayed depth remains negative at -0.360, despite improving from -0.533.

BTC funding increased from approximately 0.0081% to 0.01%, while BTC CFGI declined from 89 to 81.5 and market CFGI declined from 80.5 to 75.5. Both price and these sentiment measures softened over the capture interval.
ETH short-dated moneyness-bucket skew is negative at 1.13 and 2.13 days (-6.23 and -4.95 points). This is not 25-delta skew.
hypotheses: The strongest coherent interpretation is short-horizon consolidation or a local pullback following a strong multi-horizon advance, rather than a confirmed reversal. The negative 4h returns, lower owner marks, weaker BTC displayed depth, and softer BTC/market sentiment cohere as near-term cooling. Positive 12h-to-72h returns, broad stable breadth, and sustained ETH/BTC strength indicate that this cooling has not displaced the broader upside sequence.

The strongest falsification of the local-pullback interpretation already present in the evidence is the lack of cross-horizon and cross-family confirmation: broader returns and ETH relative performance are strongly positive, breadth has not deteriorated, and current taker quote imbalances are positive despite negative displayed depth. This configuration is also consistent with temporary liquidity-book asymmetry during an ongoing advance.

A stronger bearish regime interpretation is not supported because BTC dominance, total2, total3, stablecoin-dominance change, and comparable historical breadth persistence are unavailable; liquidation aggregates are explicitly lower bounds with unverified completeness.
summary: Detected disagreement is principally temporal and microstructural: a negative 4h move and weaker displayed liquidity coexist with positive 12h-to-72h momentum, stable broad breadth, persistent ETH/BTC strength, and positive latest taker imbalance. Supplied evidence supports only a tentative local cooling/consolidation interpretation; it does not resolve into a confirmed broader reversal.
uncertainties: The 1h sequence has one sample and zero actual span, so it is not an independent horizon.
Displayed depth and taker quote imbalance disagree for both BTC and ETH; neither establishes directional continuation on its own.
BTC and ETH open-interest changes disagree across the latest owner delta: BTC declined 0.18% while ETH increased 0.51%.
Liquidation data are lower bounds from a fragile legacy REST source, with unknown page truncation and unverified completeness.
Option readings are current-chain moneyness-bucket measures without equivalent historical snapshots and must not be interpreted as 25-delta skew.
The Binance spot owner is disabled; available spot microstructure coverage is limited to the supplied market-data capture.
BTC dominance, total2, total3, stablecoin-dominance changes, and historical breadth comparisons are unavailable and remain unknown.
